claims.text: Cover page reads "11 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009", series "Acquisition Threat Support". No DIA-08-XXXX-XXX document number is recoverable from the text layer of the released scan; it is recorded here as unknown rather than guessed.

b.label: Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human Biological Tissues

edges.label: deliverable under AAWSAP
edges.note: The released document names the programme itself. Its inside cover reads 'This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency ... Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program' - the redaction between them is (b)(3):10 USC 424. Verified by downloading this DIRD and scanning its full text on 23 August 2026. The scans are OCR-degraded, so the quotation is normalised from the damaged rendering.

a.label: Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human Biological Tissues

edges.label: authored at Wayne State University
edges.note: The DIA list gives Green's affiliation of record for this deliverable as Wayne State University. Wayne State is second only to EarthTech on the DIRD author list, supplying Green plus R. Genik's three human-interface papers.

edges.label: Biologics claim and documented injury record
edges.note: The bio claim has no released material; the medical domain has DIRD 26 and the Cash-Landrum clinical record, which is the auditable end of the same question.

edges.label: authored
edges.note: DIA list item 12 names "Dr Kit Green, Wayne State Univ", under the shorter title "Field Effects on Biological Tissues". The released document's printed title is longer and more specific.

edges.label: authored the human biological effects DIRD
edges.note: Item 12, 'Field Effects on Biological Tissues', released as 'Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human Biological Tissues' — a government document about injuries.

b.label: Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human Biological Tissues

edges.label: published and holds; document number not recoverable
edges.note: DIA commissioned, holds and released this document. It carries a DIA document number in the DIA-08-xxxx-xxx series on its cover and was released through the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room, whose FileId entry is cited here alongside the retrievable copy. Cover page read on 22 August 2026.

edges.label: The only injury case that reached federal court
edges.note: Cash v. United States arose from the December 1980 encounter on FM 1485 and was dismissed in August 1986.

edges.label: Shared clinical signature
edges.note: Dermal burn and neurological presentations attributed to anomalous encounters are also produced by directed-energy and radiofrequency exposure, which the board records rather than resolves.

b.label: Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human Biological Tissues

edges.label: series member
edges.note: Membership of the DIRD series is established by the released document itself: its cover page carries the Defense Intelligence Reference Document mark and the DIA Defense Futures banner. Publication date 11 March 2010 on the cover. 39 pages in the released copy. The cover of the scanned release is degraded, so a document number or date is asserted here only where it reads unambiguously.
